BLOCKER: AC requires a negative self-test proving "force without PF_GATE_FORCE fails"; no such test exists in gate1/gate2 self-tests or elsewhere in the diff — an explicit acceptance criterion is unmet.

gate2_completion_check/set_status never verify the evidence sha equals the CURRENT diff_sha() (gate1 has a STALE_EVIDENCE check; gate2 does not), so Gate 2 can approve against Gate 2.5 evidence for an outdated diff — the "architect diff evidence for the change sha" hard rule is not enforced.
MAJOR: core/backlog.py mutates sys.path and imports scripts/dev/architect_review (including private `ar._config()`, `ar._get_item`) inside the set_status hot path: core is now coupled to git-based dev tooling and will fail/branch differently outside a repo checkout.

gate2_completion_check honors the Gate-1 rollout baseline (ACTIVE → ALLOW), silently exempting the *completion* gate; the baseline file's own description scopes it to Gate 1 exemptions — undocumented, broader fail-open than the AC allows.

record_gate_decision enforces HIL authorization only via the `by` string prefix ("hil:"); any caller can forge `by="hil:x"`. AC requires decisions be recorded only by the HIL session — no caller identity check.

approval() ordering check (decision.at >= evidence.at) is skipped whenever evidence lacks `at` (all pre-existing evidence files) or view is None (docs-only): fail-open instead of the mandated fail-closed STALE_APPROVAL.

gate_predicates.is_docs_only is introduced as the single predicate but is dead code: `_gate2_status` and `gate2_completion_check._docs_only` each reimplement it inline — the exact duplication the "single predicate" AC forbids.
MINOR: gate1_transition_check's negative matrix is not wired with --self-test into precheck or ci-cd-gates (only gate2 is), so Gate 1 self-tests never run in CI.

record_gate_decision happily records a gate=1 decision when design evidence is absent (view None), deferring failure to the transition check — confusing and risks approvals bound to unreviewed designs.
seq = len(decisions)+1 assumes an intact journal; any edit/removal of decisions silently reuses seq numbers rather than failing append-only invariant on write.
Naive local datetimes (`datetime.now().isoformat()`) are compared as UTC in _parse_ts; ordering can be wrong across hosts/timezones.
gate2 self-test items omit `at` and `seq` fields, so the ordering/append-only branches are never actually exercised.
NIT: `_DESIGN_KEYS` duplicates the key tuple already in `_design_body` in the same file.
sys.path bootstrap block is copy-pasted across three scripts.
Observability is print-only; no structured machine-readable event sink for allow/deny or gate decisions.
SUMMARY: Solid skeleton: shared predicate module, fail-closed error paths, baseline governance, and good docs/schema work.
Two hard AC gaps block merge: missing force-override negative self-test, and Gate 2 accepting stale Gate 2.5 evidence (no current diff_sha binding).
Top risks: core→scripts/dev coupling, baseline exemptions leaking into the completion gate, and spoofable HIL authorization undermine the control-plane integrity claim.
